children: Canada is importing fewer vehicles made by U.S. automakers such as General Motors (GM), Ford (F) and Stellantis (STLA), according to data from DesRosiers Automotive Consultants.
So far in 2026, vehicle imports into Canada from the neighboring U.S. have accounted for 40% of Canada’s total when measured in terms of dollars.
That’s down nearly 10 percentage points from 49.1% of Canada’s light vehicle imports in 2024. The decline comes as tariffs make U.S. vehicles more expensive to purchase for Canadians.
Increasingly, Canada is importing vehicles from other markets around the world. The proportion of vehicle imported from Mexico increased from 16.7% in 2024 to 20.5% this year.
Vehicle imports from Japan have grown to 12.9% from 10.7%, while vehicles brought over from South Korea have risen to 12.5% from 10.4%. European imports have swelled to 11.1% from 9.8%.
For the Detroit automakers, the shift means that they can no longer rely on Canada, which has long been one of their most reliable and lucrative markets.
DesRosiers Automotive Consultants, which tracks vehicle sales in Canada, said in a statement, “What the U.S. lost in share was captured readily by the other major light vehicle exporters.”
Canada currently maintains import tariffs of 25% on all U.S. automobiles, matching the duties that America has placed on vehicles manufactured within Canada.
The situation has led to higher retail prices for vehicles sold in Canada from General Motors, Ford, and Stellantis, shifting consumer demand to vehicles made in Japan and Europe.
Trade representatives for Canada and the U.S. are currently negotiating a new trade pact between the two countries. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the talks are progressing.
However, U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened to raise tariffs on Canadian-made vehicles to 50% in January if a new trade deal is not reached by then.
The stock of GM, the largest U.S. automaker, has risen 15% in the last 12 months to trade at $83.99 U.S. per share.

title: Canada Imports Fewer U.S. Vehicles As Tariffs Raise Prices
